messages.subject: brm returns no samples for multilevel model - works ok with RStanArm
parts:
When running a varying-intercept varying-slope model with 4 factors the model appears to sample fine, but then returns the following errors after sampling:

[1] "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:"                                          
[2] "Exception: multiply: A[38] is nan, but must not be nan!  (in 'model1e9c46947686_file1e9c16d59f2' at line 72)"                                            
[3] "If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,"                  
[4] "but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."                                                
[5] "Error in sampler$call_sampler(args_list[[i]]) : "                                                                                                        
[6] "  Exception: model1e9c46947686_file1e9c16d59f2_namespace::write_array: y is not positive definite.  (in 'model1e9c46947686_file1e9c16d59f2' at line 132)"
[1] "error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done"


The model was run as:

brm_post = brm(SB ~ FlowSpeed * Presence * Fix * Bend  + (1 + FlowSpeed * Presence * Fix * Bend| pp), data = data,
               prior = set_prior("normal(0, 1)", class = "b"),
              iter = 10, cores = 1, refresh = 100, chains = 1, 
              control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99))





The same formula seems to work fine in RStanArm:

rstan_post = stan_glmer(SB ~ FlowSpeed * Presence * Fix * Bend + (1+ FlowSpeed * Presence * Fix * Bend | pp), data = data,
              family = gaussian, 
              adapt_delta = 0.99, chains = 4, cores =4, iter = 2000, refresh = 1) #This call includes most of the parameters you might want to fiddle with



Does anyone know what might be causing this behaviour? 


Many thanks.

Oscar

Hi Paul,

This reproduces the issue for me. 

I'm not sure if it could be the difference in the model formulation and priors between RStanArm and brms. But it seems strange to me that it seems to sample but then returns an error. 

I'm using R 3.4.1, brms_2.01 and rstanarm_2.17.2. Let me know if you need any more information. 

Many thanks for looking into this. 

Oscar 

library(tidyverse)
library(rstanarm)
library(ggplot2)
library(brms)

A = c("A1", "A2")
B = c("B1", "B2", "B3")
C = c("C1", "C2", "C3")
D = c("D1", "D2")
trial = c("1", "2")
subj = seq(1,20)

data = as.data.frame(expand.grid(A = A, B = B, C = C, D= D, trial = trial, subj = subj))
data$y = rnorm(dim(data)[1], 0, 1)


##RStan run works
rstan_post = stan_glmer(y ~ A * B * C* D + (1+ A * B * C* D | subj), data = data,
              family = gaussian,
              adapt_delta = 0.99, chains = 1, cores =1, iter = 500, refresh = 1)

#BRMS returns no samples
brm_post = brm(y ~ A * B * C* D + (1+ A * B * C* D | subj), data = data,
               prior = c(set_prior("normal(0, 5)", class = "b"),
                         set_prior("cauchy(0, 2)", class = "sigma")),
              iter = 500, cores = 1, refresh = 1, chains = 1,
              control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99))

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] brm returns no samples for multilevel model - works ok with RStanArm
parts:
It seems to be as if the model is heavily over-parameterized. Each combination of A, B, C, and D only have 2 observations per person. As you model (1+ A * B * C* D | subj), you have 36 parameters per person, each being barely identified by the 72 observations per person. Now consider that you have 36 random effects SD parameters as well as 36 * 35 / 2 = 630 random correlation parameters, all that with just 1440 observations in total. That's a lot.

You need stronger priors to get this to sample at all. The default priors for random effects are stronger in rstanarm than in brms, which is the reason the former is more willing to sample from your model, but still this is not a model I would recommend fitting with that few data.

That said, you can get this model to sample in brms, by adding a stronger prior on the random effects SDs, for instance

set_prior("student_t(3, 0, 2)", class = "sd")

You can also try setting inits = 0. Sometimes this helps.

Out of curiosity, my expectation was that the model would either not initialize, or return samples, even if the model is poorly identified. In this case it initialized, sampled (iteration progress outputs to console) and then finally returned the "sampling not done" error. Do you have any insights into why this might occur?

All the best

parts:
Not sure. Maybe it did only sample for some chains and not for others?

In any case, this is how Stan handles things. brms has nothing to do with this part. You may want to ask this question on http://discourse.mc-stan.org/.

2018-01-16 13:25 GMT+01:00 Oscar Giles <oscart...@gmail.com>:
Thanks Paul, that's really useful.

As you suggest, adding more data points and a tighter prior on the sd parameter resolved the issue. 



Out of curiosity, my expectation was that the model would either not initialize, or return samples, even if the model is poorly identified. In this case it initialized, sampled (iteration progress outputs to console) and then finally returned the "sampling not done" error. Do you have any insights into why this might occur?

All the best

 


On 16 January 2018 at 10:42, Paul Buerkner <paul.b...@gmail.com> wrote:
It seems to be as if the model is heavily over-parameterized. Each combination of A, B, C, and D only have 2 observations per person. As you model (1+ A * B * C* D | subj), you have 36 parameters per person, each being barely identified by the 72 observations per person. Now consider that you have 36 random effects SD parameters as well as 36 * 35 / 2 = 630 random correlation parameters, all that with just 1440 observations in total. That's a lot.

You need stronger priors to get this to sample at all. The default priors for random effects are stronger in rstanarm than in brms, which is the reason the former is more willing to sample from your model, but still this is not a model I would recommend fitting with that few data.

That said, you can get this model to sample in brms, by adding a stronger prior on the random effects SDs, for instance

set_prior("student_t(3, 0, 2)", class = "sd")

You can also try setting inits = 0. Sometimes this helps.
